plan: In a second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning and paying more than your value if the second-highest bid exceeds your value; underbidding only reduces your chance of winning without lowering the price you’d pay (which is set by others). With no history to exploit and one round, maximize expected profit by bidding exactly your value: 42.

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values and no exploitable history, the dominant strategy is to bid truthfully. Bidding my value (29) ensures I win whenever the others’ top bid is below 29 and pay the second-highest bid, guaranteeing nonnegative profit. Underbidding risks missing profitable wins; overbidding risks negative profit if I win when the price approaches or exceeds my value due to rivals’ bids. Therefore, I will bid my exact value.

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds your value, causing negative profit; underbidding risks losing when you would have gained. With value 48 and bids in $0.1 increments, I will bid exactly 48 to maximize expected profit. Ties break randomly; bidding higher doesn’t improve payment, only win probability, and truthful already optimizes that tradeoff. ]
